Consult Summary:
- 27-year-old female with 2-day history of central lower abdominal pain, mild nausea, slight haematuria and increased urinary frequency.  
- Telehealth assessment; clinician suspects uncomplicated urinary tract infection (UTI) and arranged 3-day oral antibiotic course with safety-net advice.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Suspected uncomplicated UTI / acute cystitis  
- Onset: 2 days ago.  
- Symptoms: Central lower abdominal pain, mild nausea (no vomiting), slight pink discoloration of urine, mild increase in urinary frequency, subjective thirst, feeling hot/sweaty (self-recorded temp 37 °C).  
- Pertinent negatives: No dysuria, no significant fever (>37 °C), no back/flank pain, no foul urine odor, no vaginal discharge, no upper GI reflux, bowels currently normal.  
- Differential: UTI vs early pyelonephritis (warned), vs gynecologic cause (less likely given absence of discharge or cycle change).  
- Plan: 3-day oral antibiotic course (drug name not documented; twice daily). Safety-net instructions provided.

Issue 2: Constipation last week – resolved  
- Brief episode of constipation noted the week prior; currently passing normal stool (last BM 2 h ago, no rectal bleeding).

Issue 3: Drug allergy  
- Amoxicillin allergy documented; important for antibiotic selection.

Medications:
- None regularly.  
- Planned: Oral antibiotic (name/dose/route/frequency not documented) – instructed twice daily for 3 days.

Allergies:
- Amoxicillin (reaction not specified).

Past Medical History:
- Denies chronic illnesses.  
- Family history: Mother had early-stage breast cancer (treated).

Social History:
- Lives with parents.  
- Smoking: Never.  
- Alcohol: ~1 beer, 4 times/week.  
- No recent travel.

Preventative History:
- No preventive care data (cervical screening, mammogram, vaccinations, etc.) discussed.

Physical Examination:
- Remote consultation; no in-person exam.  
- Vital: Patient-reported temperature 37 °C; other vitals not obtained.

Plan:
- Send electronic prescription for 3-day antibiotic course to patient’s nominated pharmacy.  
- Begin medication immediately on collection.  
- Advise to seek urgent review if: worsening pain, fever, back pain, vomiting, persistent haematuria, or no improvement after antibiotics.  
- Arrange face-to-face assessment if new/worsening symptoms occur or recurrence of similar episode.  
- No other concerns raised; patient declined further questions.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing expected elements: exact antibiotic name/dose/route, reaction details to amoxicillin, complete vitals, pregnancy status, last menstrual period, cervical screening/vaccination status.  
● No internal transcript conflicts noted.  
● Transcript quality acceptable; occasional unclear wording but core clinical information intact.
